title: Ruled Notebook — Humanities Seminar Lecture
description: A cream-paged, navy-ink notebook slide that faithfully mimics a humanities student's in-class notes — ruled baselines, a slightly wandering ballpoint hand, doodled connector arrows, and exactly one sun-yellow highlighter swipe over the slide's key term.
philosophy: This template refuses polish as a virtue. It exists to make information feel discovered rather than delivered — the kind of slide that signals 'I worked this out with a pen, not a design suite.' It values cognitive warmth and legible imperfection over corporate authority, inviting audiences into the thinking process rather than presenting conclusions. It is built for speakers whose credibility comes from genuine curiosity, not from visual dominance.
goodFor: Workshop concept-mapping frames with visible linking logic
Single key-term definition slides with margin annotation
Educational explainer content aimed at student or hobbyist audiences
avoidFor: Formal investor pitches or boardroom quarterly reviews
Chart-heavy data dashboards requiring precise grid alignment
Legal or compliance presentations where typographic authority matters
Brand identity launches where design precision signals credibility
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like the inside cover of a well-used seminar notebook — intimate, earnest, and imperfect in a way that signals real thinking rather than finished conclusions. Compositional drama rises from the tension between ruled-line regularity and ballpoint letterforms that drift ever so slightly off the baseline, with the sun-yellow highlighter swipe serving as the single intense focal anchor against the cream page. Avoid digital symmetry, hard drop shadows, and anything that reads as designed rather than written.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-col grid with a navy vertical margin rule sitting at col 2, leaving the left gutter open for marginal doodles and course annotations. Ruled baselines span the full width at even vertical intervals, with the deck title occupying the upper-center zone roughly a third down from the top edge. A sun-yellow highlighter rectangle underpaints the title's key term, bleeding slightly past the letterforms on both sides. A handwritten session label or course code anchors the top-right header zone, tucked above the first ruled line as a notebook-style page header.

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like a lecturer's working notes — warm, imperfect, intellectually alive. A single highlighter swipe over the key term provides the only moment of visual heat, while hand-drawn connector arrows stitch surrounding ideas into a web of live reasoning rather than a tidy list. The mood is cognitive intimacy over authority: viewers sense they are reading genuine curiosity, not curated conclusions. Lean into the slight diagonal drift of ballpoint lines and the layered quality of ideas that appear to have been recorded at different moments in the same sitting.

examples.layoutNotes: Ruled horizontal baselines span the full page width, establishing the primary vertical rhythm grid. A left margin column — roughly one-fifth of the slide width — holds doodled connector arrows, parenthetical asides, and small sketched icons pointing inward toward the main content block occupying cols 2–10 of a 12-col implicit grid. The single key term sits in the upper content zone beneath a highlighter stripe that bleeds fractionally beyond its text boundary on both sides. A small page-number or section marker anchors the lower-right corner, sitting just below the last ruled line outside the main field.
